subtopics.title: Where and Why Mid-Latitude Cyclones Form

questions.question: The mid-latitude cyclones that bring winter rain to South Africa's south coast develop:
options: Between 30 and 60 degrees south over the ocean, travelling west to east on the westerlies
Over the warm Mozambique Channel, travelling east to west
Over the Kalahari, travelling south
Along the equator, drifting poleward

questions.question: Cold polar air and warm subtropical air meet at the polar front but do not mix because:
options: The jet stream keeps them apart
They differ in density, so the cold air stays beneath and the warm air is levered upward
The ocean absorbs one of them
They only meet at night

questions.question: Because the Coriolis force deflects moving air to its left in the Southern Hemisphere, air around one of our low-pressure cells circulates:
options: Anticlockwise
Straight inward without curving
Clockwise
Outward from the centre

questions.question: The jet stream helps a mid-latitude cyclone deepen by:
options: Blowing the fronts back toward the west
Warming the air in the warm sector
Adding moisture at the surface
Dragging air away from the top of the system so surface pressure falls and more air spirals inward

subtopics.title: Stages of Development — Wave to Occlusion

questions.question: Which sequence gives the life cycle of a mid-latitude cyclone in the correct order?
options: Occlusion, mature stage, initial wave
Initial wave stage, mature stage, occlusion stage
Mature stage, initial wave, dissipation
Warm sector, cold sector, polar front

questions.question: In the mature stage, the warm sector is best described as:
options: The cold air behind the cold front
The centre of lowest pressure
The wedge of warm, humid air lying between the warm front and the cold front
The cloud band above the jet stream

questions.question: The cold-front surface slopes at about 1 in 50 while the warm-front surface slopes at about 1 in 100. The consequence is that:
options: The cold front lifts warm air fast, building cumulonimbus and violent showers, while the warm front builds layered cloud and steady rain
The warm front produces thunderstorms and the cold front produces drizzle
Both fronts produce identical weather
Neither front can produce rain

questions.question: At occlusion, the system begins to die because:
options: The jet stream reverses direction
The warm sector is lifted off the surface, cutting the storm off from its warm-air fuel
The ocean beneath it freezes
The Coriolis force stops acting

subtopics.title: Front Weather — Before, During and After

questions.question: The single most reliable signature of a cold-front passage over a south-coast town is:
options: A rise in temperature at midday
Fog forming at sunrise
The wind swinging from north-west, through west, to south-west
The barometer holding perfectly steady

questions.question: While a town still lies in the warm sector ahead of the cold front, the barometer shows:
options: Steadily falling pressure as the low centre approaches
Rapidly rising pressure
No change at all
Random jumps up and down

questions.question: South Africa seldom experiences warm-front weather because:
options: Warm fronts dissolve over cold ocean water
The country lies against the northern edge of the systems, so the warm front usually passes to the south over the ocean
The escarpment blocks all warm fronts
Warm fronts only form in the Northern Hemisphere

questions.question: Which impact is correctly paired with its management response?
options: Winter dam-filling rain — evacuate the coast
Storm swell at harbours — issue drought warnings
Snow closing mountain passes — plant windbreaks
Flooding of low-lying settlements — clear storm-water drains before the rainy season

subtopics.title: Reading the Synoptic Chart and the Satellite Image

questions.question: On a synoptic chart, an occluded front is shown as:
options: A line with solid triangles only
A line with alternating triangles and semicircles on the same side
A dashed line with circles
A double line with no symbols

questions.question: Widely spaced isobars on a synoptic chart indicate:
options: A gentle pressure gradient and light winds
Gale-force winds
Heavy rainfall
A tropical cyclone

questions.question: Frontal rain reaches the south-western parts of South Africa in winter because:
options: The ocean is warmest in winter
The jet stream stops in winter
The South Atlantic and South Indian Highs shift north with the sun, placing the storm corridor across the southern tip of the continent
Cold fronts travel westward in winter

questions.question: On a satellite image, a mature mid-latitude cyclone appears as:
options: A circular cloud disc with a clear central eye
A straight band of cloud along the equator
A completely cloud-free spiral
A comma-shaped cloud band whose tail streams north-west along the cold front

questions.question: In the picture of two crowds at a rope, the crowd in blankets and the crowd in shorts represent:
options: Cold polar air and warm subtropical air meeting at the polar front
Day and night
The two subtropical high-pressure cells
Rain and snow

questions.question: Cold air behaves like cold syrup poured into water because it:
options: Evaporates quickly
Is denser, so it slides underneath and forces the lighter warm air upward
Mixes instantly with the warm air
Rises to the top of the atmosphere

questions.question: The jet stream is compared to a chimney over a fire because it:
options: Keeps the storm warm
Pushes the storm back westward
Draws air up and away from the top of the storm, so the surface pressure keeps dropping
Adds smoke to the cloud band

subtopics.title: The Storm's Life in Three Photographs

questions.question: Photograph one — the bend in the rope — shows:
options: The occlusion stage
The initial wave stage, where friction kinks the polar front into a shallow wave
The mature stage
The dissipated storm

questions.question: In the mature stage, the escalator and the snowplough blade stand for:
options: The jet stream and the polar front
The two subtropical highs
High tide and low tide
The gentle warm front and the steep, fast cold front

questions.question: The storm fades after occlusion because:
options: The warm air that fuelled it has been squeezed up off the surface, like a fire with no wood left
It collides with a mountain range
The sea becomes too rough
The Earth stops rotating beneath it

questions.question: When drawing the mature stage, the correct chart symbols are:
options: Half-moons on the cold front and triangles on the warm front
Stars on both fronts
Triangles on the cold front and half-moons on the warm front
Dotted lines on both fronts

questions.question: On Thursday morning, before the front reaches George, the town experiences:
options: Cold south-westerly wind and rising pressure
Snow on the beachfront
Clear skies with no wind at all
Unusually warm sticky air, a north-westerly wind and a steadily falling barometer

questions.question: As the front strikes on Thursday afternoon, the beachfront flags swing around from:
options: North-west to south-west — the storm signing its name
South to north
East to north-east
South-west back to north-west

questions.question: The storm track runs over the southern coast in winter rather than summer because:
options: The ocean current reverses each winter
The whole wind system shifts north with the overhead sun, bringing the storm highway over the land
The Outeniqua mountains attract the storms
Summer air is too heavy to lift

questions.question: Which action belongs BEFORE the front arrives rather than after it?
options: Repairing roofs stripped by the gale
Measuring how much rain fell
Clearing storm-water drains and opening shelters when the warning is issued
Reopening the snowed-in mountain pass
